title: docs(spec): book.json's liveness header names the dead row, not a pair of integers
body:
Fixes #16136

Clause-②: no
  The change rewrites one prose sentence in the `_note` header of a liveness ledger.
  No accept set moves, no export is added, no schema arm, bound or behaviour changes,
  and every per-prop `status` row stays byte-for-byte as it was. `packages/spec`'s
  published surface changes only in the shipped text of `liveness/book.json`.

## The reading, re-taken on this branch's base (`50dc2141a`)

The `_note` opened with, verbatim:

> 15 of 17 live; the two dead entries are both inline `translations` maps that LOOK like the doc-level mechanism that works (`doc.translations`, resolveDocLocale) but have no resolver anywhere.

My own recount, walked at every nesting level of the ledger's own rows, with a live
control proving the parse worked:

```
top-level props:                    8   (name, label, description, slug, icon, order, audience, groups)
rows carrying a status, all levels: 14   ->  live 13 · dead 1
the one dead row:                   props.groups.children.translations
live control:                       `resolveBookTree` occurs 13x in the same read
```

The gate's own report beside it — `check-liveness.mts --json`, `types.book.byStatus`,
the counting method this ledger family documents and publishes in
`liveness/state-counts.md`:

```
book: { "classified": 21, "unclassified": 0, "byStatus": { "live": 20, "dead": 1 } }
```

which is exactly the published row `| book | 20 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 21 |`. So 15 and 17
appear in **neither** granularity — 13 of 14 by ledger rows, 20 of 21 by the gate — and
"the two dead entries" is plural where the file records one. The plural is the half a
reader acts on: it sends them hunting for a second dead inline `translations` map that
the ledger does not carry.

## The acceptance condition: did a second dead entry ever exist?

**Yes — and it was not lost.** This decides the deliverable, so it is answered with
evidence rather than assumed.

**Route taken: a complete clone.** This container's checkout is no longer shallow —
`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returns `false`, the root commit `1598cabe4`
("Initial commit", 2026-01-18) is reachable, and 13,316 commits are reachable from
HEAD — so `git log` here is a history reading. Corroborated independently of git by
the ledger README, below.

Recounting `liveness/book.json` at **every revision in its history**:

| revision | date | top-level props | rows | live | dead |
|:---|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `4f13be22b` (#4488 seeding) | 2026-08-01 | 9 | 15 | 13 | **2** |
| `7d2158146` (#4667) | 2026-08-03 | 8 | 14 | 13 | 1 |
| `3de535b86`, `9c249a69b`, `8cb96ec41` | → today | 8 | 14 | 13 | 1 |

At seeding the ledger carried a second dead row, `props.translations` (book-level inline
translations), `status: dead` with `authorWarn: true`. It was removed by `7d2158146`,
whose own commit message states the ledger discipline that governed the removal:

> `book.groups[].translations` and `app.homePageId` are TOMBSTONED (`retiredKey`: `never` at compile time, the prescription at parse time) and keep their ledger rows, because the key stays in the walked shape. … The other four are strict deletions carrying `guidance`, and their rows are deleted.

So the row is **absent because its key is absent from the walked shape**, which is
precisely what this ledger records — not lost, not merged away. Three independent
confirmations:

1. **The schema.** `BookSchema` carries only a comment where the key was
   (`// translations removed in 17.0.0 (#4667)`); `BookGroupSchema.translations` survives
   as `retiredKey(BOOK_TRANSLATIONS_RETIRED)`, which is why exactly that one keeps a row.
2. **The ledger README's own `book` row**, in writing, independent of git history:
   "**#4667**: both inline translation maps retired — book-level row DELETED (BookSchema
   is strictObject), group-level row KEPT as a tombstone".
3. **The gate.** `unclassified: 0` for `book`, and `check:liveness` enforces both
   directions — "every governed-type property at the walk's one-level granularity is
   classified … no ledger row outlives its property".

⇒ **No row is missing.** The clause-② fence does not fire: the ledger was complete all
along and only the sentence had gone stale, on the day the second key was retired. The
prose change is the whole deliverable.

Worth recording for the next reader: `the two dead entries` was **true when written** and
went false on 2026-08-03. `15 of 17` was never true at any granularity — the same PR that
seeded it published `| book | 13 | – | 2 | – |` in the README table. I did not run the
seeding-era gate to recover where that pair came from; its provenance is not established
here.

## What the replacement says, and deliberately does not

Per the family precedent (#15775) and this ledger README's counting-method section — "The
Notes cell is **not** a place to restate a number" — the new sentence states the
**boundary** and restates **no total**. Writing "13 of 14" would have reproduced this card
with a later date.

> `groups[].translations` is dead: an inline map that LOOKS like the doc-level mechanism that works (`doc.translations`, resolveDocLocale) but has no resolver anywhere. Its book-level twin was the same trap and was retired in the same pass (#4667) — that one is a strict deletion, so it left the walked shape and holds no row here, while the group-level key is TOMBSTONED (`retiredKey`; BookGroupSchema is a plain z.object with no `.strict()`) and stays in the shape this ledger walks. No total is restated in this header: `state-counts.md` publishes the counts and `check:liveness` proves that artifact fresh on every run.

The `doc.translations` / `resolveDocLocale` contrast is kept — it is real, hand-measured
content and the reason the trap works. The last clause is the anti-recurrence device: it
tells the next author why no integer is here, so one is not helpfully restored.

## Scope held

Everything outside `_note` is byte-identical (asserted mechanically during the edit: the
parsed document minus `_note` serializes identically before and after). No `status` value
moves, no schema changes, no other liveness ledger is touched, and
`liveness/state-counts.md` is **not** hand-edited — `check:liveness` reports it current,
so no regeneration was owed.

## Changeset — decided with both halves, measured

A changeset **is** owed, and the deciding tree is the published `liveness/` directory, not
`dist`.

1. **Path in `files[]`?** Yes. Measured from a real `npm pack` of `packages/spec`
   (276 files): `liveness/book.json` PRESENT; positive controls `llms.txt`, `README.md`
   PRESENT; negative control `scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts` ABSENT.
2. **Is the changed text in what ships?** Yes. Unpacked the real tarball
   (`objectstack-spec-17.3.0.tgz`) and grepped it: the new sentence is present at
   `liveness/book.json`, the old sentence is gone from the whole package. Positive
   control (pre-existing published text in the same file, "ADR-0046 §6 documentation
   spine") present; negative control `proofErrors: [] as string[]` — a string that exists
   in the working tree only inside the unpublished `scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts` —
   present in the working tree, absent from the packed tree. The probe discriminates.

## Verification

Gate families derived from the real change set with
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`
(re-derived after the changeset existed: 54 runnable commands, 6 of them new).

- **53 of 54 green.** Foremost `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:liveness` — its own
  verdict lines: "✓ every governed-type property at the walk's one-level granularity is
  classified … no ledger row outlives its property …" and "✓
  packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md is current — the same 36 row(s), no count column
  left in the README."
- **1 NOT MEASURED**, not red: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3 with
  "PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output, and some package has no dist/
  … ⛔ This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured" (87 packages unbuilt; that is a
  whole-repo build, CI's run). `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` hit the same prerequisite,
  so `@objectstack/objectql` was built and it was re-run into a real reading: "✓ 2
  published condition(s) measured from a real load."
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **467 files / 13100 tests passed**.
  `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — clean (`tsc --noEmit` +
  `check:scripts-typecheck` + `check:test-typecheck`).
- Build of the affected closure (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/spec...' build`) and both
  test/typecheck runs went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; every one printed
  `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` green, plus a direct control-byte self-scan over both changed
  files (`grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'`, no hits).
- The key families were **re-run on the final commit `542b5dbf9`** — liveness,
  empty-state, nul-bytes, published-files, merge-driver, doc-authoring, the two changeset
  gates, objectui-changeset, lean-entry-closure, adr-0087-registration — all exit 0.
- **`pnpm lint` (repo-scan) is CI's run; the local narrowing is declared and measured.**
  (i) eslint's own config declares a JS/TS-only population — every `files` block is
  `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` or narrower, with no `.json` and no `.md` block.
  (ii) `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over both changed paths: 2 results, 0
  errors, both "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied" — zero files
  of this diff are in the linted population. (iii) Type-aware linting is not enabled
  anywhere in this repo (no `parserOptions.project`, stated in `eslint.config.mjs` and
  measured there with a positive control), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any
  untouched file.

## Out of scope, noted and not filed

The liveness **README**'s `book` Notes row still opens with "Dead 2 = BOTH inline
`translations` maps" before its own "#4667:" update corrects the disposition two sentences
later — the same restated-count shape as this card, one file over, in a file this card
fences off. Left for the PM to route: the card's surface is `book.json`'s header only, and
the README is the carrier of a different family member. Successor: whoever takes the next
`liveness/README.md` prose card.
